rubber bands (to tie ten sticks into one bundle, and ten bundles into one big hundred-bundle)
meta.designNotes: Topic 1 opener. p2 Adventure Begins hook (Taleemabad library is 999 days old). p3-4 place-value walkthrough: 123 = 1 hundred, 2 tens, 3 ones; expanded form 123=100+20+3; 342 place/value; count forward 123->126 and backward 342->337 (verified). p4 Practice Questions on 602 (H/T/O, expanded form, place & value of each digit). Model with a place-value chart / base-10 blocks. [Stage-C ELEMENTS: cumulative spaced-retrieval warm-up (prior lessons); topic-fit number-sense warm-up (subitise/number-bonds
sloDescriptions: I can recognise the place value of each digit in 3-digit numbers (hundreds, tens, ones/units).
I can count numbers up to and across 999 (3-digit numbers) forwards and backwards, beginning from zero or one, or from any given number.

goal: Learn that a digit's value depends on its place -- hundreds, tens or ones.
sloFull: By the end of the lesson, students will recognise the place value of each digit in a 3-digit number (hundreds, tens, ones) and count forward and backward across 3-digit numbers.
warmUpPeerMove: Choral count by tens together, then partner-check on '10 tens = 100'.
exitSuccessCriteria: Correct if the student says DIFFERENT and explains the 7 and 0 sit in different places, worth 70 vs 7.
exitSelfPredict: Draw a smiley or sad face predicting whether 470 and 407 are the same number.

warmUp.recallOf: General prior knowledge: counting by tens (Day 1
warmUp.teacherAsks: Count by tens together from 10 to 100. Now tell your partner: how many tens make 100?

hook.story: Taleemabad's library is 999 days old! Look at these big numbers: 531, 342, 123. Have YOU seen a number this big -- on a bus, a price tag, a house number?
objects: A hundred-bundle made of ten bundles-of-ten sticks taped together, to show what '100' looks like.

conversation.teacherAsks: Have YOU ever seen a number this big before? Where?
conversation.listenFor: Names a real place (bus number, price tag, house number).

keyWords.def: single units, fewer than a bundle.
what a digit is worth because of WHERE it sits in the number.
writing a number as the sum of its hundreds, tens and ones.
one single number symbol (0-9) inside a bigger number.

board.instruction: Before class, draw a 3-column Hundreds | Tens | Ones chart. Draw bundles/sticks for each example -- never a bare digit alone.
board.content:
Hundreds | Tens | Ones
10 tens = 1 hundred-bundle
123 = 1 hundred + 2 tens + 3 ones
WORDS: digit = ہندسہ | expanded form = پھیلی ہوئی شکل | place value = پوزیشن کی قیمت

steps.action: Draw 1 hundred-bundle, 2 bundles, 3 sticks for 123 in the chart. Count each column aloud before writing any digit.
steps.say: One hundred-bundle, two bundles, three sticks. That's 1 hundred, 2 tens, 3 ones -- we write 123.
steps.sayLocal: Ek hundred-bundle, do bundles, teen sticks. Yeh 1 hundred, 2 tens, 3 ones hai -- hum 123 likhte hain.

iDo.teacherSays: The digit's VALUE depends on which column it sits in, not just its name.
iDo.teacherSaysLocal: Digit ki VALUE us column par depend karti hai jahan woh baitha hai, sirf naam par nahi.
iDo.keyFact: The same digit is worth a different amount in a different place.

worked.diagram:
342 —
3 hundreds: [bundle][bundle][bundle]
4 tens: [bundle][bundle][bundle][bundle]
2 ones: [bundle][bundle]
123 —
1 hundred: [bundle]
2 tens: [bundle][bundle]
3 ones: [bundle][bundle][bundle]

iDo.cfu: What is the value of the digit 2 in 123?
iDo.cfuPassSignal: Says 40, pointing to the four bundles.
iDo.ifStruggle: Cover the digit 2 with your hand and ask: how many bundles are still there? Count them: 2 bundles = 20.

misconception.slip: Children say the digit's name instead of its value (say '2' for the tens digit instead of '20').
misconception.why: The digit looks the same whether it sits in tens or ones, so naming feels like enough.
misconception.fix: Cover the digit and count the bundles in that column out loud before saying the value.

weDo.action: Help Zainab build 256 with bundles together.
weDo.strategy: Ask how many hundred-bundles, bundles and sticks are needed; fill the chart together before writing any digit.

partner.instruction: Digit Detective: Partner A names a 3-digit number, Partner B says its hundreds/tens/ones VALUES.
partner.a: My number is ___. What are its hundreds, tens and ones?
partner.teacherRole: circulate, listening for VALUE not just digit-naming; reset a pair's streak with encouragement, never a penalty.

weDo.cfu: Which digit in 256 tells us the TENS, and what is its value?

youDo.action: Complete p.4's Practice Questions on 602 independently.

wordProblem.prompt: Ali has 602 rupees saved. Write 602 in expanded form to show hundreds, tens, ones.

behind.prompt: Build 130 with bundles: how many hundred-bundles, bundles and sticks?
behind.coach: Let the child lay out the bundles first, then count each column before writing the digit.

ahead.prompt: Write 602 and 620 in expanded form. Which digit moved, and what happened to its value?
ahead.answer: 602=600+0+2; 620=600+20+0 -- the 2 moved from ones to tens
ahead.coach: Push the child to say WHY the value changed, not just which number looks bigger.

exitOptions.prompt: Is 470 the same as 407? Explain using place value.
exitOptions.promptLocal: Kya 470, 407 kay barabar hai? Place value se batao.
exitOptions.answer: No -- different; the 7 and 0 sit in different places (tens vs ones)
exitOptions.howToRun: Each child writes their answer; ask 2-3 to explain aloud.

exitOptions.prompt: Which number has a 5 in the TENS place?
exitOptions.promptLocal: Konsay number mein 5, TENS jagah par hai?
exitOptions.howToRun: Read all 4 aloud; children circle one; thumbs up when done.
Each child writes in notebook; glance-check as they finish.

keyFacts: The same digit is worth a different amount in a different place.
Ten tens make one hundred; ten ones make one ten.
homework: p.4-style: Bilal's number 385 -- write H/T/O, expanded form
wrap.reflection: Could children state a digit's VALUE, not just its name, without prompting?
